title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E08 — The League of Corinth
Philip's defeat of Greece is matched only by the diplomatically ingenious settlement of his newly conquered territories; the ruler's strategies for running his empire; one of his most impressive administrative projects; the League of Corinth.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E01 — South America's Lost Cradle of Civilization
The evidence for South America as one of the true wellsprings of human civilization; the diversity of early South American cultures; what the cultures shared; innovations in agriculture, architecture, handicrafts, social organization and religion.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E02 — Discovering Peru's Earliest Cities
The first cities in the Americas, dating back to 3000 B.C.; investigating the means of subsistence of coastal and inland valley cities; evidence of trade in marine and agricultural products; learning about the sites of Kotosh, El Paraíso and Caral.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E03 — South America's First People
The earliest evidence of humans in the Americas; Monte Verde and its view into ancient life.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E04 — Ceramics, Textiles, and Organized States
Observing pivotal changes in northern Peruvian societies; architectural styles; a state identity.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E05 — Chavín and the Rise of Religious Authority
How the site of Chavin marks the emergence of religion as the focus of public art; Chavin's architecture, with images of its characteristic fanged deity; later religious iconography and artifacts suggesting that Chavin was the center of a cult.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E06 — Cupisnique to Salinar - Elite Rulers and War
The waning of Chavin's culture; new elements in the Chavin region's archeological record; encountering the Salinar culture; a settlement pattern showing no ceremonial architecture; the first elite housing; evidence of defensive citadels.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E07 — Paracas - Mummies, Shamans, and Severed Heads
Investigating the Paracas tombs of the first millennium B.C., which contain richly adorned mummies; the significance of mummification; the elaborate iconography of Paracas textiles and the meaning of the supernatural beings they depict; headhunting.

title: Lost Worlds of South America
description:
S01 E08 — The Nazca Lines and Underground Channels
The Nazca and their accomplishments; the Nazca's irrigation system of underground aquifers, aqueducts and wells; polychrome pottery and textiles; the mystery of the Nazca Lines, which may be the result of ritual pilgrimage.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Alexander the Great - Conqueror or Tyrant?
Pondering Alexander's identity and story; learning about the ancient sources that contribute to people's understanding of Alexander's life and legacy; examining the ways this figure is perceived by modern scholars.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E02 — Greece in the Age of Hegemonies
The story of Alexander starts centuries before his birth, in the Greek city-states throughout the Aegean; the conflicts and political crises that shape the Greek world in the generations before Alexander; his father Philip's conquest of the region.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E03 — Achaemenid Persia
The Persian Empire of the 4th century offers a fierce opponent to Alexander in his conquest; the history of this mighty empire in the two centuries before Alexander's rise; the political and administrative structures that contribute to its success.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E04 — The World of Early Macedon
Although they ultimately unite Greece, Philip and Alexander are not considered full-fledged Greeks, learning about their barbarian homeland of Macedon and investigating its relationship to the more culturally influential city-states of Greece.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E05 — Philip II and the Macedonian Way of War
In his victories, Alexander is indebted to his father, Philip II, for his remarkable innovations in warcraft; Philip's achievements, including his reorganization of the Macedonian army; a study of three decisive battles.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E06 — The Third Sacred War
A turning point in Greek political history; the Third Sacred War, a conflict that pits major powers in Sparta and Thebes in a battle for dominance; the complicated negotiations in this conflict that lead to Philip's control of Delphi and the Aegean.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E07 — The Macedonian Conquest of Greece
By 346 B.C., Philip of Macedon congratulates himself on some stunning victories; his greatest achievement is yet to come: the ingenious political and military maneuvers, the decisive Battle of Charonea, which gives Philip control of the Greek world.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E08 — The League of Corinth
Philip's defeat of Greece is matched only by the diplomatically ingenious settlement of his newly conquered territories; the ruler's strategies for running his empire; one of his most impressive administrative projects; the League of Corinth.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E01 — How Washington DC Came to Be
Uncovering the origins of the District of Columbia; how the location for the national government is chosen; the original design and vision for the city by artist and engineer Pierre Charles L'Enfant; the creation and history of the National Mall.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E02 — The White House and the Presidency
Tracking the history and fortunes of the White House; visiting the White House, beginning with the Oval Office and Cabinet Room; visiting the parks adjoining the White House; the Jefferson and Franklin Delano Roosevelt memorials.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E03 — The Capitol Building and the Legislature
How the Capitol building is designed, constructed and expanded in the early years of the nation; touring the architectural and artistic wonders of the building; concluding with the House and Senate Chambers; the surrounding parks and gardens.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E04 — The Supreme Court and the Law of the Land
Studying the founding and history of the Supreme Court; touring this structure, its interior features, court facilities and artistic decoration; exploring the Court in action, which encompasses courtroom procedure and how cases are processed.

title: The Great Tours: Washington D.C.
description:
S01 E05 — The Nation's Knowledge: Library of Congress
Visiting the world's largest library; the story of the library's creation in the 18th century; beginning with the Jefferson Building; the facilities of the Adams and Madison buildings; visiting the Folger Shakespeare Library; the Eastern Market.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E01 — Reflections On and of Pompeii
When most people hear the name of the archeological site of Pompeii, they think of destruction; gaining an overview of the course; considering why the remains of Pompeii offer more than just a story of a cataclysm.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E02 — Geology and Geography On the Bay of Naples
Land and humankind help to shape Pompeii; examining the violent geological forces that forge the distinctive region of the Bay of Naples; tracing its influence on the surrounding geography; the various cultures that contribute to life in this area.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E03 — The Rediscovery of Vesuvian Lands
Archeological finds from the area are unearthed starting around 1594; uncovering the history of Pompeii's excavation in the 1700s, from the kings who plunder its artwork to the modern scholars who seek another kind of treasure.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E04 — Etruscan Pompeii - 5th Century B.C.
While the last days of Pompeii attract popular attention, the city is a thriving cultural center centuries before its destruction; delving deep into Pompeii's remote Etruscan history; exploring what life is like in this ancient pre-Roman settlement.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E05 — Samnite Pompeii - 2nd Century B.C.
Centuries after the establishment of Etruscan Pompeii, the city is invaded by the Samnites; witnessing the conquest of the city by these invaders; considering how Pompeii is redefined and expanded by its new inhabitants.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E06 — Building the Roman Colony - 80 B.C.
Encountering the first Roman inhabitants of Pompeii; learning how Pompeii becomes a Roman colony; taking a tour of the city as viewed through the eyes of two of its chief magistrates.

title: The World's Greatest Churches
description:
S01 E01 — The Earliest Churches
Considering what defines a church; encompassing its religious uses and its functions as a place of assembly; how the first churches come into being; studying some of the best surviving basilica-type churches in Italy; their structural features.

title: The World's Greatest Churches
description:
S01 E02 — The Church of the Holy Sepulchre
Tracing the history of this church in the Holy Land; the medieval reconstruction seen today; the church's unusual structure, which incorporates the "aedicule"; individual chapels reflecting events of the passion of Christ.

title: The World's Greatest Churches
description:
S01 E03 — Hagia Sophia
Learning about the past of this jewel of Constantinople; discovering an extraordinary architectural space; highlighting its dome and interiors; lingering over its mosaics, carved columns and decoration in colored marbles.

title: The World's Greatest Churches
description:
S01 E04 — The Cave Churches of Cappadocia
Pondering the unusual churches of Turkish Cappadocia, elaborately carved into the sides of mountains; the lives of the monks and hermits who live there; studying the churches' frescoes that illustrate biblical scenes and the life of Jesus.

title: The World's Greatest Churches
description:
S01 E05 — Great Churches of Russia
The beauties of the churches of the Russian Orthodox tradition; the religious culture that inspires these structures; their characteristic gilded domes; their decoration of sculpture, frescoes and tile work; visiting outstanding cathedrals.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E01 — Muslim Empires: Land, Language, Religion
The geographical region known as Greater Middle East; the range of nations and cultures that define it; historical turning points to witness, encompassing conquests, political alliances and Islam's rise; social, intellectual and economic reforms.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E02 — Muhammad and the Dawn of Islam - 622
Islam's rise is a major turning point; tracing key phases in the life of Muhammad (PBUH); the founding of the faith through his years of opposition; his establishment of Islam as a religious and political entity; the global impact of these events.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E01 — From Camels to Stars in the Middle East
One of the most important yet overlooked periods in human history; the who, what, why, where, when and how of the Golden Age of Islamic Civilization; exploring the Abbasid Empire; how it bridged the ancient world and the Renaissance.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E02 — Ibn Battuta's Search for Knowledge
Meeting the Moroccan wayfarer Ibn Battuta; tracing his journey across Northern Africa and the Middle East in the century after the Mongol sack of Baghdad; new insights into the era, including whether it ever truly come to an end.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E01 — A Meeting of Two Worlds
Introducing the themes of increasing American power; indigenous political aspirations; conflicting interests and goals; growing mutual antagonism; setting the stage for World War I.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E02 — Wilson & the Breakup of the Ottoman Empire
An examination of wartime and postwar American policy; showing how Wilson's commitment to an ethnocentrically defined view of national self-determination drives his efforts to shape the postwar settlement in the Middle East.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E01 — Uncovering Near Eastern Civilization
Egypt, Greece and Rome may be better known to the public; more written evidence survives from Mesopotamia; embarking on a journey through over 3,000 years of history; learning why Mesopotamia's rediscovery is so valuable.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E02 — Natufian Villagers and Early Settlements
The enormous value of plant and animal domestication; the theories about the transition from a hunter-gatherer lifestyle to agriculture; the challenges that farming presents; a perspective on the cultural sophistication of pre-agrarian peoples.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E01 — The Land of Canaan
What is meant by "holy land"; the difference between archeology and history; how reliable the Hebrew Bible is as a window into life in ancient Israel; answers to these and other questions; the region's earliest recorded inhabitants, the Canaanites.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E02 — The Arrival of the Israelites
What archeologists uncover about the arrival of the Israelites into Canaan; an ancient Egyptian stele with the earliest reference to Israel; the remains of Jericho's walls; a Philistine temple similar to the one Samson destroys in the book of Judges.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E01 — The New Testament-An Overview
The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E01 — Biblical Israel - The Story of a People
Entering the world of biblical Israel with a historical overview; an examination of how the Bible gives insights into the daily life of ancient Israelites; considering the context for how the Bible comes into being.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E02 — By the Rivers of Babylon - Exile
A look at the Babylonian exile; the exiled Judeans begin asking themselves who they are as a people and why they are conquered; as the Bible begins to be compiled in this time of exile, it offers two vantage points for understanding its history.

Entering the world of biblical Israel with a historical overview; an examination of how the Bible gives insights into the daily life of ancient Israelites; considering the context for how the Bible comes into being.

title: The World of Biblical Israel
description:
S01 E02 — By the Rivers of Babylon - Exile
A look at the Babylonian exile; the exiled Judeans begin asking themselves who they are as a people and why they are conquered; as the Bible begins to be compiled in this time of exile, it offers two vantage points for understanding its history.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E01 — Muslim Empires: Land, Language, Religion
The geographical region known as Greater Middle East; the range of nations and cultures that define it; historical turning points to witness, encompassing conquests, political alliances and Islam's rise; social, intellectual and economic reforms.

title: Turning Points in Middle Eastern History
description:
S01 E02 — Muhammad and the Dawn of Islam - 622
Islam's rise is a major turning point; tracing key phases in the life of Muhammad (PBUH); the founding of the faith through his years of opposition; his establishment of Islam as a religious and political entity; the global impact of these events.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E01 — From Camels to Stars in the Middle East
One of the most important yet overlooked periods in human history; the who, what, why, where, when and how of the Golden Age of Islamic Civilization; exploring the Abbasid Empire; how it bridged the ancient world and the Renaissance.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E02 — Ibn Battuta's Search for Knowledge
Meeting the Moroccan wayfarer Ibn Battuta; tracing his journey across Northern Africa and the Middle East in the century after the Mongol sack of Baghdad; new insights into the era, including whether it ever truly come to an end.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E01 — A Meeting of Two Worlds
Introducing the themes of increasing American power; indigenous political aspirations; conflicting interests and goals; growing mutual antagonism; setting the stage for World War I.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E02 — Wilson & the Breakup of the Ottoman Empire
An examination of wartime and postwar American policy; showing how Wilson's commitment to an ethnocentrically defined view of national self-determination drives his efforts to shape the postwar settlement in the Middle East.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E01 — Uncovering Near Eastern Civilization
Egypt, Greece and Rome may be better known to the public; more written evidence survives from Mesopotamia; embarking on a journey through over 3,000 years of history; learning why Mesopotamia's rediscovery is so valuable.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E02 — Natufian Villagers and Early Settlements
The enormous value of plant and animal domestication; the theories about the transition from a hunter-gatherer lifestyle to agriculture; the challenges that farming presents; a perspective on the cultural sophistication of pre-agrarian peoples.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E01 — The Land of Canaan
What is meant by "holy land"; the difference between archeology and history; how reliable the Hebrew Bible is as a window into life in ancient Israel; answers to these and other questions; the region's earliest recorded inhabitants, the Canaanites.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E02 — The Arrival of the Israelites
What archeologists uncover about the arrival of the Israelites into Canaan; an ancient Egyptian stele with the earliest reference to Israel; the remains of Jericho's walls; a Philistine temple similar to the one Samson destroys in the book of Judges.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E01 — The New Testament-An Overview
The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

Entering the world of biblical Israel with a historical overview; an examination of how the Bible gives insights into the daily life of ancient Israelites; considering the context for how the Bible comes into being.

The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E03 — The Pauline Epistles
This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E04 — The Problem of Pseudonymity
This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

description:
S01 E01 — Uncovering Near Eastern Civilization
Egypt, Greece and Rome may be better known to the public; more written evidence survives from Mesopotamia; embarking on a journey through over 3,000 years of history; learning why Mesopotamia's rediscovery is so valuable.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E03 — Neolithic Farming, Trading, and Pottery
Travel is dangerous but people transport valuable goods, perhaps via chains of merchants; daily life in Neolithic Mesopotamia, where homes and villages reflect a simple society; evidence of intricate pottery shows that people care about aesthetics.

title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
description:
S01 E04 — Eridu and Other Towns in the Ubaid Period
The Ubaid people construct monumental buildings, standardize some measurements and must have some sort of formal leadership to care for and control their populations; the people of the Ubaid coordinate their efforts to develop irrigation systems.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E01 — From Camels to Stars in the Middle East
One of the most important yet overlooked periods in human history; the who, what, why, where, when and how of the Golden Age of Islamic Civilization; exploring the Abbasid Empire; how it bridged the ancient world and the Renaissance.

description:
S01 E02 — Ibn Battuta's Search for Knowledge

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E03 — Arabian Nights Caliph: Harun al-Rashid
Getting to know Caliph Harun al-Rashid; Baghdad's House of Wisdom, which is the largest depository of books in the world at the time; it serves as the engine that drives much of the Golden Age; the Arabian Nights collection of stories and legends.

title: The History and Achievements of the Islamic Golden Age
description:
S01 E04 — The Arab World's Greatest Writer: al-Jahiz
Considered by many scholars to be the finest writer of Arabic prose to ever live, Al-Jahiz is a stylist and author of more than 200 works, uncovering the origins of Arabic writing and documenting the life and works of Al-Jahiz.

description:
S01 E01 — The Land of Canaan

description:

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E03 — Jerusalem - An Introduction to the City
Surveying the topography and layout of Jerusalem; reviewing biblical accounts of Jerusalem from the arrival of David around 1,000 B.C.E. to the start of the Babylonian exile in 586 B.C.E.; the remains of an Assyrian siege on the city of Lachish.

title: The Holy Land Revealed
description:
S01 E04 — The Jerusalem of David and Solomon
A first look at the biblical City of David; combing through the remains of a scribe's house behind a city wall; the development of biblical Hebrew script; rare examples of this script in a clay sealing, a piece of pottery and a victory stele.
